name: Whot Nigerian
description: Nigerian variant of Whot: a shedding game in the Eights family. Players match suit or number or play Whot (wild) and special cards (Hold On, Pick Two, Pick Three, Suspension, General Market). First to empty hand wins; penalty scoring over rounds. Popular in West Africa.

overview.description: Nigerian variant of Whot: a shedding game in the Eights family. Players match suit or number or play Whot (wild) and special cards (Hold On, Pick Two, Pick Three, Suspension, General Market). First to empty hand wins; penalty scoring over rounds. Popular in West Africa.

history.origins: Whot was invented by W.H. Storey in England in 1935 and became the national card game of Nigeria. Nigerian variant uses the same 54-card pack with local names for shapes (ball, angle, cross, carpet, star) and added special effects on 1, 2, 5, 8, and 14.
timeline: 1935: Whot! invented and trademarked by William Henry Storey, Southend-on-Sea, England; first marketed by Storey & Co of Croydon.
1930s-1940s: Game acquired by Waddingtons of Leeds; 54-card pack with five Whot cards standard.
1950s-1960s: Popular in Britain; Waddingtons sold until the 1990s.
Nigeria: Adopted as national card game; local suit names (ball, angle, cross, carpet, star) and special effects on 1, 2, 5, 8, 14 added; 54-card pack retained.
history.cultural: Became the national card game of Nigeria; widely played across West Africa. Local names for suits (ball, angle, cross, carpet, star); optional rules include time limits per turn and direction change on 2 or 5.
history.evolution: British version had no special card effects beyond matching suit or number and wild Whot. Nigerian variant added Hold On (1), Pick Two (2), Pick Three (5), Suspension (8), General Market (14), semi-last and last card announcements, and check-up penalty.

setup.deck: A 54-card Whot pack with five pictorial suits (circles, triangles, crosses, squares, stars) and five wild Whot cards numbered 20; this format is standard in Nigeria. Suit cards carry numbers 1–14 (not all numbers in every suit); star cards count double for scoring.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles; player to dealer's right cuts. Dealer deals six cards to each player one at a time. Remainder forms a face-down draw pile (stock).

rules.objective: Be the first to get rid of all your cards. Others score penalty points for cards left in hand; players with 100 or more drop out; last player left wins.
rules.gameplay: On your turn play one card matching the top card's suit or number, or play a Whot and name a suit. If you cannot or do not wish to play, draw one card from the stock (you may not play after drawing that turn). Nigerian specials: 1 Hold On (play again), 2 Pick Two, 5 Pick Three, 8 Suspension (skip next; Star 8 skips two), 14 General Market (all others draw one). Say semi-last card and last card; say check up when playing last card or draw two as penalty.
keyRules: Match suit or number of the top card, or play Whot and name a suit
If you cannot or do not wish to play, draw one from stock; you may not play after drawing that turn
When stock is empty, shuffle all but the top card of the play pile to form a new stock
First to empty hand wins; others score penalty points; 100+ drops out

strategy.basic: Match suit or number when possible; save Whot and special cards for when you have no match or to attack.
strategy.intermediate: Keep 2s and 5s to defend against Pick Two and Pick Three; play them when opponents hold few cards to slow them.
strategy.advanced: Use Whot to demand a suit you hold or one an opponent likely lacks; play high-value cards first to minimise penalty if you do not win.
tips: Announce semi-last and last card and check up to avoid penalty.
Star 8 skips two players; use it when the next player is close to winning.

variations.name: Short game
variations.description: One deal only; first player to empty hand wins, no penalty scoring.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Short game has no engine overrides; one deal only, first to empty hand wins.

scoring.description: First to empty hand wins; others score penalty points (face value, stars double, Whot 20); 100+ drops out.

synthesis.shortDescription: Nigerian variant of Whot: match suit or number, use special cards, first to empty hand wins.
